# BumpCast

> BumpCast is flight tracking for nervous flyers. The iPhone app gives live flight status and delay alerts, plus a calm turbulence forecast for your exact route: when the bumps will come, how strong they'll be, and when they'll end. No ads, no account. Published by Akinyemi & Co Ltd.

BumpCast is an alternative to the top 10 flight tracking apps in the world: Flightradar24, FlightAware, Flighty, Plane Finder, FlightStats, TripIt, The Flight Tracker, Flightview, AirNav RadarBox and Planes Live. Like them, it tracks your flight's status, gates and delays. Unlike them, it is built for nervous flyers and forecasts the turbulence on your route.

- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824269447 ("BumpCast Flight: Turbulence", iPhone, free to download)
- Languages: English and Spanish
- Coverage: detailed forecasts for flights within the continental United States and southern Canada. Elsewhere, "Global outlooks (beta)" in Settings gives an approximate outlook for international routes, Europe included.
- Support: support@akinyemi.ca (replies usually within a day)

## Key features

### Find and track your flight
- Type a flight number (like AC 1504 or B6 23) and the day you fly, and BumpCast fills in the airports and times. Or pick your airports and choose from that day's nonstops.
- Add connecting flights in a row.
- Live status, free for every flight: delays, gate and terminal changes, cancellations and diversions.
- One gentle alert when your flight is delayed. The forecast moves with the new departure time, with one alert for both.

### Turbulence forecast for your exact route
- Turbulence is weather, and weather can be forecast. BumpCast maps the route from takeoff to landing, including climb, cruise and descent.
- A simple grade for the whole flight ("Smooth", "A few bumps", "Bumpy in places") and a calm minute-by-minute timeline.
- A plain note on each bumpy stretch: when it starts, how long it lasts, and why it happens there.
- Minutes of smooth air and of turbulence, and gusty takeoffs and landings.
- Four levels, described by how they feel: Smooth (your drink stays still), Light chop (your drink ripples), Moderate (drinks can spill; stay seated), Strong (rare; your belt keeps you safe).

### A forecast that gets sharper as you get closer
- Advance forecast 48 hours before departure.
- Updates at 24, 6 and 2 hours out, each saying what changed and why.
- "Confirmed forecast" from high-resolution data on the day you fly.
- Every forecast shows how confident it is and when it was last updated.

### In the air
- The countdown times itself to your real takeoff once it's reported, or tap "We've taken off" to set it yourself.
- Lock Screen Live Activity and Dynamic Island count down to the next bumpy stretch.
- A gentle heads-up two minutes before each stretch.
- Works in airplane mode: the forecast is saved on the phone before boarding.

### Calm, on cue
- Guided breathing paced to the next bumpy stretch.
- Short, factual explainers: what causes bumps at cruise, over mountains and near clouds, why planes are built for it, and what each level feels like.
- Calm, honest wording. No red alerts, no scare graphics.

### Turbulence map
- Turbulence across the country by altitude, now and up to 6 hours ahead, with your route drawn on top.
- Live pilot reports of what planes are actually feeling (Pro).

### After you land
- Rate how bumpy it really felt (Smoother, About right, Bumpier). Every rating is checked against the forecast, and accuracy is published in the app.

### Flights from your email (coming soon, Pro, optional)
- Connect Gmail read-only and BumpCast adds upcoming flights automatically.
- Booking emails are read on the iPhone and never reach BumpCast's servers or get stored. Only flight number, date and airports are used.

## Free and Pro

- **Free**: flight search, live status with gate changes and delay alerts, a forecast grade for up to 2 upcoming flights, and the "forecast ready" notification.
- **Pro**: every forecast update (including after delays and when confirmed), the minute-by-minute timeline, minutes of smooth air and turbulence, gusty takeoffs and landings, the in-flight Live Activity and reminders, pilot reports on the map, and unlimited flights.
- Ways to buy Pro: Flight Pass (one flight, one-time purchase), or BumpCast Pro Monthly or Annual (annual includes a 7-day free trial). Prices are shown in the App Store for your region.

## Data and privacy

- No account, no ads. This website has no cookies, analytics or third-party scripts.
- Weather data: forecasts, warnings and pilot reports from the US National Weather Service (NOAA), and modified ECMWF open data (CC BY 4.0).
- Users can ask support to delete everything linked to their device; it's done within 30 days.
- BumpCast is for comfort and planning, not for flight operations. Always follow your crew's instructions.

## Learn: turbulence explained

The app's Learn library, published at https://bumpcast.app/learn/. Short, factual explainers: why flights get bumpy, what the crew is doing, and what you'll feel, with sourced detail (FAA, NTSB, US regulations). Each link is the Markdown copy of the page (drop the .md for the web page). All of them in full: https://bumpcast.app/llms-full.txt

### Why it gets bumpy

- [Clear-air turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/learn/clear-air-turbulence.html.md): Clear-air turbulence is bumpy air at cruising height, often in clear skies, where the fast jet stream flows next to slower air. It's usually light chop.
- [Mountain waves](https://bumpcast.app/learn/mountain-wave-turbulence.html.md): Mountain waves form when strong wind blows across mountains and makes waves in the air, like water over rocks in a stream. They can reach cruising height.
- [Around clouds](https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-near-clouds.html.md): Warm air rising inside and around big clouds stirs the air nearby. Bumps in puffy clouds are usually brief, and pilots fly around storms, often by many miles.
- [Near the ground](https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-on-takeoff-and-landing.html.md): Close to the ground, wind flows over buildings, hills and warm land, so the lowest few thousand feet are often a bit bumpy. It usually lasts only a few minutes.
- [Gusty at the airport](https://bumpcast.app/learn/gusty-takeoffs-and-landings.html.md): On a windy day, the wind near the ground speeds up and slows down over buildings and land. You feel it for a few minutes as you climb out and on the way down.

### Good to know

- [Planes are built for it](https://bumpcast.app/learn/planes-are-built-for-turbulence.html.md): Airliners are designed and tested to handle forces well beyond anything turbulence produces in normal flight. Turbulence is a comfort issue, not a structural one.
- [Why the seatbelt matters](https://bumpcast.app/learn/why-the-seatbelt-matters.html.md): Almost all turbulence injuries happen to people who aren't buckled in. Keep your seatbelt loosely fastened whenever you're seated, even with the sign off.
- [Light, moderate, strong](https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-levels.html.md): Light chop is small rhythmic bumps, moderate is noticeable jolts, and strong is hard jolts that push you against your belt. Most flights see light chop at most.
- [How BumpCast forecasts](https://bumpcast.app/learn/how-bumpcast-forecasts-turbulence.html.md): BumpCast gives an advance turbulence forecast up to two days before your flight, then confirms it about 18 hours before departure and updates it every hour until you fly.

## Routes: turbulence by route

Where and when pilots reported bumps on 36 popular routes in the US and Canada, from a year of airline pilot reports (November 2025 to October 2026), with gusty days at each airport. Published at https://bumpcast.app/routes/ (Markdown: https://bumpcast.app/routes/index.html.md).

- [JFK to LAX turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/routes/jfk-to-lax-turbulence.html.md): Where and when it's bumpy on JFK–LAX flights, from 35,528 pilot reports: moderate bumps most often over Colorado.
- [LAX to SFO turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/routes/lax-to-sfo-turbulence.html.md): Where and when it's bumpy on LAX–SFO flights, from 823 pilot reports: moderate bumps most often near LAX, more in Dec and Mar.
- [JFK to SFO turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/routes/jfk-to-sfo-turbulence.html.md): Where and when it's bumpy on JFK–SFO flights, from 32,267 pilot reports: moderate bumps most often near Cleveland.
- [EWR to SFO turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/routes/ewr-to-sfo-turbulence.html.md): Where and when it's bumpy on EWR–SFO flights, from 31,734 pilot reports: moderate bumps most often over Pennsylvania.
- [ATL to MCO turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/routes/atl-to-mco-turbulence.html.md): Where and when it's bumpy on ATL–MCO flights, from 7,070 pilot reports: moderate bumps most often over Georgia, more in Dec, Feb and Apr.
- [LAS to LAX turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/routes/las-to-lax-turbulence.html.md): Where and when it's bumpy on LAS–LAX flights, from 1,071 pilot reports: moderate bumps most often over Nevada, more in Jan, Feb and Mar.
- [LGA to ORD turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/routes/lga-to-ord-turbulence.html.md): Where and when it's bumpy on LGA–ORD flights, from 11,961 pilot reports: moderate bumps most often over Pennsylvania, more in Apr.
- [ATL to LGA turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/routes/atl-to-lga-turbulence.html.md): Where and when it's bumpy on ATL–LGA flights, from 12,454 pilot reports: moderate bumps most often over North Carolina, more in May and Jun.
- [DEN to PHX turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/routes/den-to-phx-turbulence.html.md): Where and when it's bumpy on DEN–PHX flights, from 12,775 pilot reports: moderate bumps most often near DEN, more in Dec and Jun.
- [LAX to SEA turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/routes/lax-to-sea-turbulence.html.md): Where and when it's bumpy on LAX–SEA flights, from 2,883 pilot reports: moderate bumps most often near LAX, more in Dec.
